language.script_notes: English as national — this is the most densely populated and most-covered part of Australia.
false_friends: New Zealand's North Island (similar suburban development)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: NSW/ACT guardrails often end with a yellow background and black diagonal dash — a useful sub-regional tell within this profile.
road_furniture.curb_style: As national; denser, more formal suburban infrastructure than the Outback or remote WA.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Victoria uses circular concrete utility poles with a distinctive 'mountain-shaped' bracket structure that looks vaguely European; Queensland's tropical north has elevated Queenslander-style housing visible along many roads.

architecture.roof_style: Single-story pitched-roof suburban houses dominate; elevated stilt-house 'Queenslander' architecture appears in tropical Queensland specifically.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal roofing widespread; terracotta tile common in older Sydney/Melbourne suburbs.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick veneer suburban houses dominate NSW/Victoria; timber Queenslander houses raised on stilts (for flood/heat/ventilation) common in Queensland.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Warm brick and pale weatherboard in the south; light timber tones on elevated Queenslander houses further north.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Dense brick-veneer suburban housing around Sydney/Melbourne; elevated timber Queenslander houses in Brisbane and further north; the Sydney Harbour/CBD skyline as an unmistakable landmark where visible.

nature.vegetation: Lush eucalyptus forest and subtropical/tropical rainforest increasingly further north into Queensland; well-watered green suburban lawns and street trees in the cities.
nature.terrain: A relatively narrow, densely populated coastal strip backed by the Great Dividing Range; the terrain and vegetation become noticeably greener and more tropical moving from Melbourne north to Brisbane/Cairns.
nature.climate_signature: Temperate in Victoria/southern NSW, increasingly humid subtropical/tropical toward Queensland — the greenest, most developed part of the country.

vehicles.plate_color: NSW commonly yellow plates; Victoria blue/white; Queensland maroon/white — plate colour alone often identifies the specific state within this region.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: As national; heaviest overall vehicle density given this region holds most of Australia's population.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Best and most current coverage in the country, concentrated around Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense, near-complete coverage — most 'generic Australia' Street View imagery comes from this region.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The East Coast is green, densely developed and suburban; the Outback is red-dirt, sparsely vegetated and largely empty of buildings.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Left-hand traffic, similar suburban brick/weatherboard housing, English signage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Australia's bollard red reflector stops partway around the post vs. New Zealand's full wrap; New Zealand's terrain is hillier and greener with more visible mountains.
